hypothesis: The catalog has two distinct valid T1 programs: the coalesced one-output-per-thread control averaged 0.0234084 s, while the 16x32-output, K-depth-32 tile averaged 0.0228994 s. That small observed difference does not establish a tiling benefit. This contrasting 8x32-output, K-depth-16 tile keeps a full warp on contiguous output columns while using 256 threads per CTA; it tests whether a smaller row tile and CTA help occupancy, against the costs of less row reuse and more K-loop synchronization. Correctness and repeated timing remain for the controller to evaluate.
notes: The supplied prior T1 measurements are the comparison points; this candidate has not been measured. The source retains the run entry point, default-stream launch, scratch-buffer behavior, alpha/beta update, tail masking, and full-FP32 arithmetic. No controller correctness or speed result is claimed.
transformations: Changed the CTA output tile to 8 rows by 32 columns with one output per thread and lanes spanning contiguous columns.
Staged A and B cooperatively in synchronous shared memory with K depth 16; masked input tails and synchronized before and after accumulation.
Retained the existing entry point, default-stream launch, alpha/beta semantics, and unused scratch buffer; added no allocation or external math-library call.
